invariants: Decision.approval_status == 'approved' and Decision.approved_by matches ^human(:<name>)?$ for every record (only a human approval creates a record; records never self-authorize, ADR-060)
Decision.staged_at == Decision.approved_at (staging is automatic: the run stages the record the moment the human approves)

Decision.staged_path == '<run_root>/runs/' + run_id + '/staged/decisions/' + id + '.yaml' for every record (every record is staged in its run before it can be published); a record may write the run part as the placeholder <run_id>, which stands for its own run_id
Decision.lifecycle_stage == 'staged' iff Decision.record_path == null iff Decision.review_state == 'not-published'
Decision.record_path == 'docs/decisions/' + id + '.yaml' iff Decision.lifecycle_stage in {published, superseded}
Decision.publish_pr == null when Decision.review_state == 'not-published'

Decision.lifecycle_stage == 'superseded' iff Decision.superseded_by != [] iff Decision.corrections != [] (only `decisions publish --correct` supersedes a record, appending one correction per superseding record and changing nothing else)
Decision.superseded_by contains B iff record B.supersedes contains this Decision.id, and each correction's superseded_by names one of them
Decision.selected_option_id resolves to one of its options[].id, and Decision.selected_option_title equals that option's title
Decision.title == Decision.selected_option_title, shortened by the kernel with ' ...' when long

Decision.assessment_basis == 'precedent_reuse' iff exactly one precedents_considered entry has action 'reused'; such a record has criteria == [], selected_rank == null, confidence == null, and its single option is proposed_by 'precedent:<that id>'

Decision.assessment_basis == 'kernel_ranking' implies the options' kernel_rank values are 1..n without gaps, required_mean does not increase with rank, selected_rank == the selected option's kernel_rank, and confidence == that option's required_mean

Decision.precedents_considered[].action follows applicability: below 0.5 -> not_applicable; 0.5 or above -> used_as_evidence; 0.8 or above is offered for reuse only when the decision had no options of its own and the precedent is not superseded, and the human's answer turns the note into reused or set_aside
Decision.related == the precedents_considered ids whose action != 'not_applicable'
Decision.supersedes contains P iff its precedents_considered note for P has action 'set_aside' and the human chose a different option than P did
No Decision cites a superseded precedent with action 'reused' (a superseded record is never offered for reuse)
Decision.considered_by lists exactly the records whose precedents_considered names this id, with that record's action (a derived reverse view for display, not a field of the record file)
Decision.publish_command == 'python -m kernel decisions publish --run-id ' + run_id, followed by ' --correct <id> --reason "..."' for each id in Decision.supersedes

Decision.split_part == {decomposition, part} iff that Decomposition part's decision_id == this Decision.id (a derived reverse view for display, not a field of the record file); null for a record not formed from a split
Decomposition.parts has 2 to 5 entries, with ids unique within the record (a split proposes 2-5 bounded sub-questions)

Every Decomposition.parts[].covers is a verbatim substring of Decomposition.subject_text, and no Decomposition.dropped[].covers is (the conversion drops a proposal whose quote is not in the subject); dropped == [] when proposed_by == 'claude_code'
Decomposition.parts[].depends_on names only other part ids of the same record, with no cycles
Decomposition.found_at == 'routing' iff Decomposition.work_item_depth == 0 iff Decomposition.trigger != null (jev_none, ambiguous and bundled_accepted are all routing-time triggers at depth 0)

Decomposition.state == 'proposed' iff gate_answer == null iff every part.review == 'proposed'; such a record has every outcome 'not_run', gate_by == null, report_lines == [] and run_status == 'waiting_human'

Decomposition.state == 'rejected' iff gate_answer == 'rejected' and trigger in {jev_none, ambiguous}; such a record has every part.review == 'rejected', every outcome 'not_run', run_status == 'blocked' and report_lines saying plainly that nothing was decided (only these rejected splits end the run blocked)

Decomposition.state == 'rejected_kept_whole' iff gate_answer == 'rejected' and (trigger == 'bundled_accepted' or found_at == 'mid_run'): rejecting the split keeps the subject or work item whole. Such a record has every part.review == 'rejected' and every outcome 'not_run'. The subject or item goes ahead as ONE decision or research step, exactly as without a split, so run_status is never 'blocked' because of the split. A Decision record may result: whole_decision_id names it once formed. report_lines say plainly that it was kept whole

Decomposition.whole_decision_id != null implies state == 'rejected_kept_whole'; it resolves to a Decision record in this dataset whose question == subject_text and run_id == the record's run_id, and whose split_part == null (no part decided it)

Decomposition.gate_answer == 'approved' implies every part.review in {kept, edited, left_out}, with at least one part not left_out. Among the parts not left out: state == 'approved' when all are still pending; 'in_progress' when some have an outcome and some are still pending; 'completed' when all are settled; 'ended_partial' when none is pending and at least one did not settle (not_settled, or not_run because it waited for one)

Decomposition.state == 'ended_partial' implies run_status == 'partial': when an approved part cannot settle, the parts that do not wait for it still run, and the run ends partial, never completed (user rule, 2026-10-05)

Decomposition.parts[].outcome == 'not_settled' iff stop_reason != null (budget_stop, blocked, capability_gap or cancelled). Such a part ran: its run_id == the record's run_id. It has decision_id == null, result_ref == null and settled_order == null

Decomposition.parts[].waited_for != null iff the part is kept or edited, its outcome is 'not_run', and the run went past it. waited_for names a part in its own depends_on whose outcome is not_settled, or not_run for the same reason, so a chain of dependants each names the part it waited for. Otherwise an approved part is never not_run

Decomposition.not_covered[] lists proposals beyond the five-part cap: each covers is a verbatim substring of subject_text, reason == 'beyond the five-part cap', and its id differs from every part id. not_covered != [] only when parts has exactly 5 entries. Such entries are shown at the gate read-only and are never approved or run

Decomposition.capability_gap_recorded == true iff state == 'rejected' or proposed_by == 'claude_code'. A rejected split of a turned-away request (jev_none or ambiguous) still records the capability gap, as today (user rule, 2026-10-05). The hand split's run recorded its gap before any split existed. A split the kernel offered and that was approved, kept whole or not yet answered records no gap for the subject

No Decomposition has as its subject a caller-supplied decision request (input_payload_schema leafcutter.decision_request.v1, which names its own question, options and criteria): such a request is never checked for bundling or split (user rule, 2026-10-05)
Decomposition.gate_by matches ^human(:<name>)?$ iff Decomposition.gate_answer != null (only a human answers a split; never a model)
Decomposition.parts[].review == 'edited' iff proposed_text != null; a part whose review is proposed, left_out or rejected has outcome 'not_run'
Decomposition.parts[].outcome == 'decided' iff decision_id != null; that Decision record has question == the part's text and split_part == {decomposition: the record's id, part: the part's id}
Decomposition.parts[].outcome == 'answered' iff child_capability == 'research' and result_ref != null and findings != null
Decomposition.parts[].outcome == 'settled_by_human' iff human_answer != null; such a part has run_id == null and decision_id == null (the human answered directly, so no record exists)

Decomposition.parts[].settled_order != null iff outcome in {decided, answered, settled_by_human}; within a record the orders are 1..n without gaps, and a part settled in a run comes after every part it depends on (children run in dependency order)

Decomposition.proposed_by == 'host.decompose_goal' implies every part with a run_id has run_id == the record's run_id (children are work items of the run that split), and each decided part's Decision.precedents_considered names the decision_id of every part decided before it (an earlier child's result is precedent evidence; its applicability still sets the action)

Decomposition.proposed_by == 'host.decompose_goal' and state in {in_progress, completed, ended_partial} implies report_lines holds one line per part, starting with the part id and naming its outcome; a not_settled part's line names its stop_reason, and a waiting part's line names the part it waited for

Decomposition.proposed_by == 'claude_code' implies report_lines == [] (the run report knows nothing of a split made outside the kernel), and each part settled in a run ran as its own run, started by hand

fields.id: string — kernel-minted record id, dec-<16 hex>; the file name in docs/decisions/
fields.title: string — the record's title as filed: the selected option's title (the kernel shortens a long one with ' ...')
fields.question: string — the question the run decided (trimmed from the record's `question`)
fields.lifecycle_stage: enum: staged | published | superseded — staged == only in the run root, awaiting `decisions publish`; published == written into docs/decisions/ with the index regenerated; superseded == published, then corrected by a later record via `publish --correct`. Being reused as precedent is not a stage: see considered_by
fields.review_state: enum: not-published | in-review | merged — where the published record stands in normal git review (not-published while staged)
fields.publish_pr: string | null — the pull request carrying the published record through review (e.g. '#979'); null while staged, and on illustrative records
fields.assessment_basis: enum: kernel_ranking | precedent_reuse — kernel_ranking == formed by research, Jev's per-criterion assessment and a human ranked choice; precedent_reuse == formed by the human confirming a precedent offered for reuse
fields.criteria: array of { id, priority: required | supporting, question } — the criteria the human approved while forming (empty for a reuse)
fields.options: array of { id, title, proposed_by: caller_goal | host.generate_options | claude_code[:<role>] | human:<name> | precedent:<dec id> | null, kernel_rank: integer | null, required_mean: number | null, required_passed: integer | null, required_total: integer | null } — listed in kernel rank order; rank fields are null for a reuse. claude_code[:<role>] == submitted by the orchestrating Claude Code session (e.g. claude_code:basis_review_prototype); null == listed in the question text and filed without an author, as dec-93c1c730463c1f3c records it
fields.selected_rank: integer | null — the kernel's rank of the chosen option (null for a reuse); a human may choose below rank 1
fields.confidence: number | null — the chosen option's required-criteria mean (null for a reuse)
fields.approval_status: enum: approved — every record is human-approved
fields.approved_at: string — ISO-8601 UTC time of the human approval
fields.staged_at: string — ISO-8601 UTC time the run staged the record (provenance.created_at)
fields.precedents_considered: array of { id: dec id, applicability: number 0..1, action: used_as_evidence | offered_for_reuse | reused | set_aside | not_applicable, note } — earlier records the run's precedent search judged for this decision
fields.considered_by: array of { id: dec id, action } — later records whose precedents_considered names this one (derived reverse view: how this record was retrieved as precedent)
fields.related: array of dec ids — precedents judged applicable
fields.supersedes: array of dec ids — earlier records this decision replaces (the human decided anew and chose differently)
fields.superseded_by: array of dec ids — later records that replaced this one
fields.corrections: array of { corrected_at, corrected_by: human:<name>, reason, superseded_by: dec id, new_selected_option_id } — append-only, written by `publish --correct`
fields.components: array of component ids from docs/components.json (retrieval filter)
fields.roadmap_phase: array of roadmap phase ids (retrieval filter)
fields.repository_wide: boolean — retrieval filter: applies across the whole repository
fields.run_id: string — the kernel run that formed and staged the record (run-<16 hex>)
fields.langfuse_trace_id: string — the run's Langfuse trace id
fields.staged_path: string — where the run staged the record; <run_root> is the machine-local kernel run root, and <run_id> (where written) is the record's own run_id
fields.record_path: string | null — docs/decisions/<id>.yaml once published; null while staged
fields.publish_command: string — the command a human runs to publish this record from its run (with --correct for each record it supersedes)
fields.split_part: object | null — { decomposition: Decomposition.id, part: part id }: the part of a split this record answers (derived reverse view from Decomposition.parts[].decision_id, for display; not a field of the record file); null for a record not formed from a split
fields.source: string — where this sample record comes from: a real published or staged record, or an illustrative one for a state the real store has not reached

records.question: Decide the storage format for reusable decision criteria (the decision basis the kernel reuses across decisions). Today each run's criteria are generated per decision and stored only inside docs/decisions/dec-*.yaml records. The format must be Git-reviewable, projectable into Neo4j, and carry what clustering and reuse need.

criteria.question: Does the option name the unit a human approves and give it a path like decision records have: staged in the run root, entered into Git only by a human-run publish, never created directly from Langfuse or a mined candidate (ADR-060, ADR-058)?
Are category, decision_type and components top-level plain-YAML fields whose values come from declared vocabularies that validation enforces (ADR-061 section 4)?
Can the ADR-062 projector read the store as one reviewed native kind with canonical ids, without changing how the existing Decision kind is read?

Is category membership kept in one place outside the published decision records, so merging, splitting or moving a criterion edits only category data, with retired ids resolvable through a replaced-by link?
Does the format keep outcome and success statistics out of Git and expose only stable ids that ADR-065's derived Neo4j aggregates can key on?

Does every stored criterion or category get a repository-unique, stable id with a declared kind under ADR-061's (repository_id, kind, id) key, with validation that rejects duplicates and dangling references?
Are usage counts produced only by a generator from published records and checked for freshness like docs/decisions/index.json?
Do the existing readers of docs/decisions keep working without a change?
Can a later run find candidate criteria or categories by filter and by criterion wording without opening every file?
Can the format ship without a new config/paths.json surface or pre-commit hook?

fields.id: string — stable slug for this sample split. The kernel's id scheme for splits is not settled yet (KernelDecomposeMultiPartGoal ticket)
fields.subject_kind: enum: goal | research_request | decision_question — what was split: a caller's goal, a research request holding several needs, or a multi-part decision question met inside a run. The split is not tied to goals
fields.subject_text: string — the compound item as submitted, verbatim (whitespace normalised); each part quotes the span it covers from it
fields.found_at: enum: routing | mid_run — routing == noticed when the run's root was routed: no capability fit the compound subject (jev_none, ambiguous), or one fit but the subject bundles several decisions (bundled_accepted); mid_run == a work item below the root held several questions
fields.trigger: enum: jev_none | ambiguous | bundled_accepted | null — what started the split at routing. jev_none == no_match with reason jev_none; ambiguous == an ambiguous gap; bundled_accepted == routing accepted the subject as one decision, but it bundles several decisions, so the split is offered anyway (user decision, 2026-10-04). null when found mid_run. Only a compound subject is split: a single bounded question that no capability can handle gets no Decomposition and stays a capability gap. A caller-supplied decision request (leafcutter.decision_request.v1) is never checked for bundling or split
fields.work_item_depth: integer — depth of the work item holding the subject: 0 for the root (found_at routing), 1 or more mid_run
fields.run_id: string — the kernel run holding the subject (run-<16 hex>)
fields.run_status: enum: waiting_human | waiting_host | blocked | partial | completed — that run's status as this sample shows it (kernel RunStatus); partial == some approved part did not settle
fields.langfuse_trace_id: string — that run's Langfuse trace id
fields.proposed_by: enum: claude_code | host.decompose_goal — claude_code == drafted by hand by the orchestrating Claude Code session, outside the kernel. That is the only real path on 2026-10-02. host.decompose_goal == the kernel's host operation from the KernelDecomposeMultiPartGoal ticket. It is not built yet
fields.gate_answer: enum: approved | rejected | null — the human's answer to the proposed split; null while the gate is open. Edits and a picked subset show per part (review), under approved. What rejected leads to depends on where the split came from: a jev_none or ambiguous subject ends the run blocked; a bundled_accepted subject or a mid-run item is kept whole and goes ahead as one decision or research step (user decisions, 2026-10-05)
fields.gate_by: string | null — human:<name> who answered; never a model
fields.gate_at: string | null — ISO-8601 UTC time of the answer; null while open, or when a hand split left no time
fields.gate_note: string | null — the human's words at the gate (a rejection reason, why a part was left out, the order picked)
fields.state: enum: proposed | approved | in_progress | completed | ended_partial | rejected | rejected_kept_whole — proposed == awaiting the human; approved == accepted, no part has an outcome yet; in_progress == some approved parts have an outcome, others are pending; completed == every approved part settled; ended_partial == no part is pending, and at least one approved part did not settle (not_settled, or not_run because it waited for one), so the run ended partial; rejected == the human turned down the split of a jev_none or ambiguous subject, and the run ended blocked; rejected_kept_whole == the human turned down the split of a bundled_accepted subject or a mid-run item, and it goes ahead as one decision or research step
fields.whole_decision_id: dec id | null — the Decision record the subject or item was decided as after a rejected_kept_whole split; null in every other state, while that one decision is not formed yet, and when the item went ahead as a research step
fields.capability_gap_recorded: boolean — the run recorded a capability gap for the subject itself (not for a part). true when the person rejected the split of a turned-away request (jev_none or ambiguous): the run still records the gap, as today (user rule, 2026-10-05). Also true for the hand split, whose run recorded its gap before any split existed. false otherwise: a split is not counted as a capability gap
fields.parts: array of { id, text, proposed_text: string | null, covers, depends_on: [part ids], child_capability: decision | research, review: proposed | kept | edited | left_out | rejected, outcome: not_run | pending | decided | answered | settled_by_human | not_settled, settled_order: integer | null, run_id: string | null, decision_id: dec id | null, result_ref: string | null, findings: string | null, human_answer: string | null, stop_reason: budget_stop | blocked | capability_gap | cancelled | null, waited_for: part id | null } — 2 to 5 bounded parts in proposed order. text == the bounded sub-question or need, in the caller's words where possible (after any human edit); proposed_text == the text as proposed, kept only when the human edited it; covers == the span of subject_text the part covers, quoted verbatim; pending == approved, not settled yet; decided == a child decision staged a record (decision_id); answered == a research child returned findings (result_ref, findings); result_ref == the research child's invocation id (inv-<16 hex>), whose result lives at <run_root>/runs/<run_id>/artifacts/result-<result_ref>.json; settled_by_human == the human answered it directly outside any run, so no record exists (human_answer, verbatim); not_settled == the part ran but did not settle; stop_reason says why (its decision reached its budget stop, ended blocked, hit a capability gap, or was cancelled); not_run == never started (left out, the split is still proposed or was rejected, or the part waited for a part that did not settle, which waited_for names); settled_order == 1 for the part settled first; run_id == the run that settled it
fields.dropped: array of { text, covers, reason } — proposals the conversion dropped because their quote is not found in subject_text. They are shown at the gate read-only, each with its reason; they cannot be approved or run (always [] for a hand split)
fields.not_covered: array of { id, text, covers, reason } — proposals beyond the five-part cap. Unlike dropped[], their quotes ARE in subject_text. Only five parts are offered; these are shown at the gate read-only as not covered by this split, with reason 'beyond the five-part cap', can be asked again as a request of their own, and are never approved or run
fields.report_lines: array of string — the run report's split section: one line per part naming its outcome, or the plain lines of a rejected split; [] while the gate is open, and for a hand split (the run report knows nothing of a split made outside the kernel)
fields.source: string — real (the hand split of 2026-10-02) or illustrative (host.decompose_goal is not built yet)

records.subject_text: For the kernel we often use similar decision basis and we should also reuse them. So it would be cool to not only store decisions, but also to be able to reuse categories. As a start we can probably mine them from langfuse, and we can should put them into a new file type (needs evaluation), and then also into neo4j. And we must make sure that we are able to cluster them somehow. That way we only need LLMs to generate further categories if jev thinks some are missing to make better decision

provenance.note: The ONE canonical Decision dataset for decision_kernel (decision-lifecycle product truth). Four records mirror the real decision store: the first record (published, merged in PR #978, reused and cited as precedent), the two records published for review in PR #979, and one record staged by a precedent reuse and never published. Long text is trimmed; evidence lists, per-criterion scores and repository revisions are left out. Two records marked illustrative cover the superseded state, which no real record has reached yet. Extend this dataset; do not start a second Decision dataset.

used_by.flows now lists the four decision-lifecycle sub-flows (decision-forming, decision-staging, decision-publishing, decision-retrieval) beside the parent decision-lifecycle; each sets mock_data_ref to this dataset. No records or fields changed.

Extended in place for splitting a compound item into bounded parts. The item may be a goal, a research request with several needs, or a multi-part decision question met inside a run. Parts run in dependency order (KernelDecomposeMultiPartGoal ticket). New entity Decomposition, with five records. One is real: the hand split of the goal of run-40d2159630bb48bd (G1 decided, G3 settled by the human, G2 open). Four are illustrative, one per state host.decompose_goal would produce: proposed at the gate, with one proposal dropped for a missing quote; a mid-run decision question approved with an edit and a subset, then completed; a research request completed; a rejected split that ends the run blocked. Three Decision records added: the real staged dec-93c1c730463c1f3c (G1) and two illustrative child decisions. The later child cites the earlier as precedent. Decision gains split_part, a derived reverse view that is null on every earlier record. options[].proposed_by now also admits claude_code[:<role>] and null, as dec-93c1c730463c1f3c records them. Same id, version 2 -> 3.

User decision of 2026-10-04: a bundled request is also offered as a split when routing would accept it as one decision. Decomposition.trigger gains bundled_accepted, a routing-time trigger at depth 0. The found_at and trigger descriptions and the found_at invariant now say so. They also state that a single bounded question no capability can handle gets no Decomposition and stays a capability gap. One illustrative record added: dcp-decision-records-bundled, on the real goal of run-5d246775f5e54f11 (Finding 5 of docs/analysis/2026-10-01-kernel-trace-review-decision-records-run.md), proposed at the gate. No existing record changed. The version stays 3 because this branch has not shipped v3 yet.

User decisions of 2026-10-05: rejecting the split of a bundled_accepted subject, or of an item found mid-run, keeps it whole. It goes ahead as one decision or research step, and the run is not blocked. Only a rejected jev_none or ambiguous split still ends the run blocked. The state enum gains rejected_kept_whole, and the rejected invariant is now scoped to the jev_none and ambiguous triggers. New field Decomposition.whole_decision_id links the one Decision that may result; it is null on every record. run_status gains waiting_host. dcp-decision-records-bundled moved from proposed to rejected_kept_whole. Version 3 -> 4.

Gaps the BA found in v4 (ccd51a52, DK-400a to DK-400f), plus three user rules of 2026-10-05. parts[].outcome gains not_settled, for a part that ran but did not settle, with stop_reason (budget_stop, blocked, capability_gap, cancelled). not_run stays for parts that never started; a dependant of an unsettled part names it in waited_for. State gains ended_partial, and run_status gains partial: the other parts still run. New not_covered[] holds proposals beyond the five-part cap, whose quotes are in the subject. New capability_gap_recorded is true for a rejected split of a turned-away request (and for the hand split), false otherwise. New invariant: a caller-supplied leafcutter.decision_request.v1 is never checked for bundling or split. Every existing record gained the new fields (null, false, [], or true where a gap was recorded). Added dcp-reusable-criteria-partial (DK-400e-4) with its decided part dec-a41c07e9b35a1d62, and dcp-decision-records-seven-parts (DK-400c-1-i). Version 4 -> 5.
